claims.text: The starting material is an undoped FCC/BCC FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy-alloy protective coating.
The starting coating has a conventional grain-boundary structure.
Tungsten is a refractory-metal alloying addition.
Adding a small amount of tungsten and applying a tailored thermal treatment will promote tungsten segregation to grain boundaries.
Tungsten segregation will produce a grain-boundary complexion or thin stabilizing intergranular film.
The tungsten-enriched grain-boundary structure will suppress grain-boundary sliding.
The tungsten-enriched grain-boundary structure will reduce dislocation nucleation or motion.
Suppressing grain-boundary sliding and dislocation activity will delay or mitigate progressive creep deformation.
Sub-yield continuous loading at elevated temperature up to approximately 0.6 Tm encourages grain-boundary diffusion processes.
Relative to the undoped baseline, the tungsten-doped coating will show a marked reduction in creep strain.
Relative to the undoped baseline, the tungsten-doped coating will have a higher stress threshold for creep activation.
Reduced creep deformation will coincide with altered grain-boundary chemistry and structure in the tungsten-doped coating.
The undoped FeCoNiCrAl coating undergoes creep deformation under the stated stress and temperature conditions.
Enhanced creep resistance is expected only during sustained high-temperature loading up to 0.6 Tm at sub-yield stress.
Within the proposed operating boundary, grain-boundary diffusion is sufficient to support segregation without triggering other high-temperature degradation processes.
